title: DEMONSTRATION / behavior test — quantitative social science

units_of_analysis: Hourly retail workers; worker-level measurements nested within stores or employers
phenomena_or_topics: Schedule predictability and intention to remain with the current employer
relationships_or_questions: Which dimensions of schedule predictability are measured, and over what recall period?
How are intentions to stay or leave operationalized, including their time horizon?
How do adjusted and unadjusted associations vary by study design and worker or workplace context?
What selection, reverse-causation and measurement limitations constrain interpretation?
contexts: Retail employment; distinguish store formats, employment contracts and labor-market settings
geographic_scope: No geographic restriction proposed; retain jurisdiction and labor regulation context
scope.temporal_scope: No publication-year restriction proposed; record data-collection period and distinguish contemporaneous from longitudinal measurements
languages: Proposed initial English screening; other languages flagged for human translation decision
source_types: Original quantitative surveys, panel studies and workplace evaluations with separable retail-worker results

subquestions: Which dimensions of schedule predictability are measured, and over what recall period?
How are intentions to stay or leave operationalized, including their time horizon?
How do adjusted and unadjusted associations vary by study design and worker or workplace context?
What selection, reverse-causation and measurement limitations constrain interpretation?

concept_definitions.definition: Advance notice, stability of scheduled hours, and employer-initiated last-minute changes; distinguish predictability from total hours and worker-controlled flexibility
concept_definitions.label: schedule predictability

concept_definitions.definition: Stated intention to stay with the current employer; turnover intention is coded with its original direction and is not observed retention
concept_definitions.label: retention intentions

concept_definitions.definition: Employees paid by the hour in retail establishments; mixed-sector samples need separately extractable retail results
concept_definitions.label: hourly retail workers

include: Original quantitative evidence jointly measuring schedule predictability and current-employer retention or turnover intentions among hourly retail workers
Mixed-sector or mixed-pay samples only when relevant subgroup results are extractable
Cross-sectional and longitudinal designs retained separately, with measurement and adjustment information recoverable from full text
exclude: Actual turnover alone without an intention measure
Hours quantity, wages or flexibility alone without a predictability dimension
Non-retail or salaried-only samples without an eligible subgroup; commentary without original quantitative evidence

databases: Proposed: employment and social-science bibliographic index
strategy_groups: Combine scheduling synonyms with retail-worker terms, then add intention terms as a precision variant; compare coverage before choosing final syntax
Plan backward and forward tracing from eligible sources only after authorized discovery; retain all association directions
